correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 and 1<=m<n, diagonal degree n and off-block all-ones matrix reduce the grounded spectrum to n±sqrt((n-m)^2-j^2); boundary cases are nI. Monotonicity in |j| gives sharp allocations. The fixed-cardinality hypergeometric distribution has exactly variance m(n-m)/(2n-1). Its CLT and exact rationalization give (rho/4) chi-square with uniform integrability of two moments from sub-Gaussian sampling tails, hence error-function persistence window. A strictly positive principal eigenvector proves extinction even at the equality of logistic linearization, and positive sub- and supersolutions and strict subhomogeneity give positive persistence when r/D exceeds the threshold. Actual bundled check.py passed 864 direct finite matrix comparisons and 120 exact hypergeometric probability checks.

value.rationale: Fixed-cardinality sink design on a two-community habitat is a natural ecological boundary-location question: it changes the exact viability threshold despite identical habitat size and total degrees. The exact optimum-to-worst allocation range is O(n) for any fixed nontrivial sink fraction, whereas random allocations have a universal O(1), non-Gaussian chi-square excess and a closed-form, nondegenerate error-function persistence window. The latter is a motivated finite-size risk invariant in a near-critical demographic-free model, not just a table of small eigenvalues or a numerical novelty claim. The result supplies a reproducible benchmark and explicitly delimits its symmetry and scaling assumptions.
